article.title: Volt Typhoon exploits Fortinet FortiOS CVE-2024-21762 to maintain access to US critical infrastructure
article.summary: The PRC-aligned actor tracked as Volt Typhoon is exploiting an unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability in Fortinet FortiGate appliances (CVE-2024-21762) to compromise edge devices and pivot into operational technology networks. Mandiant observed living-off-the-land lateral movement, credential dumping from LSASS, and the deployment of webshells on the VPN appliance. C2 traffic was observed to 185.225.74.10 and the domain login-portal-update.com. SHA256 of the dropped beacon: 3b8e7d9c2f1a0b6d4e5f9a8b7c6d5e4f3a2b1c0d9e8f7a6b5c4d3e2f1a0b9c8d.
article.raw_text: Volt Typhoon exploits Fortinet FortiOS CVE-2024-21762 to maintain access to US critical infrastructure The PRC-aligned actor tracked as Volt Typhoon is exploiting an unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability in Fortinet FortiGate appliances (CVE-2024-21762) to compromise edge devices and pivot into operational technology networks. Mandiant observed living-off-the-land lateral movement, credential dumping from LSASS, and the deployment of webshells on the VPN appliance. C2 traffic was observed to 185.225.74.10 and the domain login-portal-update.com. SHA256 of the dropped beacon: 3b8e7d9c2f1a0b6d4e5f9a8b7c6d5e4f3a2b1c0d9e8f7a6b5c4d3e2f1a0b9c8d.

hypotheses.title: Initial access via CVE-2024-21762 affecting Fortinet FortiOS
hypotheses.statement: A threat actor has attempted to obtain initial access to our environment by exploiting CVE-2024-21762 in Fortinet FortiOS within the last 30 days.
hypotheses.rationale: Archetype 'initial_access_cve' selected based on CVEs cited: CVE-2024-21762; malware families: Cobalt Strike; threat actors: Volt Typhoon; vectors: exploit, vpn-edge; products: Fortinet FortiOS.

objectives.title: Inventory exposure to Fortinet FortiOS
objectives.falsification_criterion: If zero internet-facing assets run a vulnerable build of Fortinet FortiOS, the external-exploitation hypothesis is disproven for CVE-2024-21762.
objectives.suggested_query: asset_inventory | where product == 'Fortinet FortiOS' and exposure == 'internet' and version in (vulnerable_versions)

objectives.title: Hunt for exploit attempts at the edge
objectives.falsification_criterion: If WAF / firewall / IDS show no exploit-signature hits for CVE-2024-21762 in the last 30 days, in-the-wild exploitation against us is unsupported.
objectives.suggested_query: edge_logs | where signature contains 'CVE' or uri matches /exploit-pattern-for-CVE-2024-21762/ | summarize count() by src_ip, dst_host

objectives.title: Patch-status correlation
objectives.falsification_criterion: If MDM / patch-management shows 100% deployment of the CVE-2024-21762 fix across exposed hosts, the hypothesis is disproven by remediation.
objectives.suggested_query: patch_state | where kb in (fixes_for('CVE-2024-21762')) | summarize coverage = avg(installed) by host_role

objectives.title: Post-exploit web-shell sweep
objectives.falsification_criterion: If a sweep of webroots and IIS/Apache process trees finds no anomalous children (cmd, powershell, /bin/sh) on Fortinet FortiOS hosts, post-exploit foothold is unsupported.
objectives.suggested_query: process | where parent in ('w3wp.exe','httpd','nginx','java') and child in ('cmd.exe','powershell.exe','/bin/sh','/bin/bash')

objectives.title: Honeypot / canary check
objectives.falsification_criterion: If exposed canary instances of the same product show no probing or exploitation telemetry, opportunistic mass-exploitation against the org is unlikely.
objectives.suggested_query: canary_events | where product == '<product>' | where event_type in ('probe','exploit') | summarize by src_ip

hypotheses.title: Endpoint execution of Cobalt Strike
hypotheses.statement: One or more endpoints in the estate have executed or attempted to execute Cobalt Strike payloads since the reporting date.
hypotheses.rationale: Archetype 'malware_execution' selected based on CVEs cited: CVE-2024-21762; malware families: Cobalt Strike; threat actors: Volt Typhoon; vectors: exploit, vpn-edge; products: Fortinet FortiOS.

objectives.title: EDR hash sweep for Cobalt Strike
objectives.falsification_criterion: If a search of EDR file/process telemetry for known Cobalt Strike SHA256s returns zero hits in the last 90 days, payload presence is disproven.
objectives.suggested_query: process_events | where sha256 in (ti_lookup('Cobalt Strike', 'sha256')) | summarize count() by host

objectives.title: Behavioural pattern hunt for Cobalt Strike
objectives.falsification_criterion: If parent/child anomalies typical of the family (e.g. Office spawning script hosts, rundll32 chains) are absent across the estate, execution chain is unsupported.
objectives.suggested_query: process | where parent in ('winword.exe','excel.exe','outlook.exe') and child in ('rundll32.exe','wscript.exe','mshta.exe','powershell.exe')

objectives.title: Persistence-key inspection
objectives.falsification_criterion: If autoruns, scheduled tasks, services, and WMI subscriptions show no Cobalt Strike-aligned artifacts, post-execution persistence is disproven.
objectives.suggested_query: registry_set | where key matches /Run|RunOnce|Image File Execution Options/ and value matches /unusual-path/

objectives.title: AV / quarantine retrospective
objectives.falsification_criterion: If retrospective AV / quarantine logs show no detections for related signatures over the last 30 days, the family is unlikely to have landed in-environment.
objectives.suggested_query: av_events | where signature contains 'Cobalt Strike' | summarize by host, action

objectives.title: Memory-resident loader check
objectives.falsification_criterion: If a memory scan (YARA via EDR / Volatility) finds none of the published loader patterns on a sampled set of high-risk hosts, in-memory residency is unsupported.
objectives.suggested_query: memory_scan | yara_rule == 'rule_cobalt_strike' | summarize by host

hypotheses.title: Outbound C2 beaconing to reported infrastructure
hypotheses.statement: Hosts in the estate are beaconing to the command-and-control infrastructure reported in this article (domains, IPs, TLS fingerprints, or RMM tooling).
hypotheses.rationale: Archetype 'c2_beacon' selected based on CVEs cited: CVE-2024-21762; malware families: Cobalt Strike; threat actors: Volt Typhoon; vectors: exploit, vpn-edge; products: Fortinet FortiOS.

objectives.title: DNS resolution sweep for published C2 domains
objectives.falsification_criterion: If recursive DNS logs show zero resolutions for the IOC domains in the last 90 days, active beaconing is disproven.
objectives.suggested_query: dns | where query in ('login-portal-update.com') | summarize count() by client_ip

objectives.title: Egress connections to published C2 IPs
objectives.falsification_criterion: If proxy / firewall egress logs show no connections to the IOC IPs or matching ASNs, network-level C2 is unsupported.
objectives.suggested_query: egress | where dst_ip in ('185.225.74.10') | summarize bytes_out = sum(bytes_sent) by src_ip

objectives.title: Beacon periodicity / jitter analysis
objectives.falsification_criterion: If beacon-style periodic outbound connections (low jitter, small payloads) to uncategorised destinations are absent, covert C2 is unlikely.
objectives.suggested_query: conn | summarize stddev_interval = stdev(diff(ts)), count() by src_ip, dst_host | where count() > 50 and stddev_interval < 5s

objectives.title: TLS / JA3 fingerprint pivot
objectives.falsification_criterion: If JA3/JA3S fingerprints associated with the reported family are absent in TLS telemetry, encrypted C2 attribution is weakened.
objectives.suggested_query: tls | where ja3 in (ti_lookup('family','ja3')) | summarize by src_ip, sni

objectives.title: Remote-monitoring tooling abuse check
objectives.falsification_criterion: If unmanaged AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installs are absent, RMM-based C2 is disproven.
objectives.suggested_query: process | where name in ('anydesk.exe','teamviewer.exe','screenconnect.exe','atera*.exe') and signer != 'corp_managed'

hypotheses.title: Post-foothold lateral movement consistent with Volt Typhoon
hypotheses.statement: An attacker who matched the TTPs of Volt Typhoon has moved laterally inside the estate using RDP/SMB/WinRM, admin tooling, or Kerberos abuse.
hypotheses.rationale: Archetype 'lateral_movement' selected based on CVEs cited: CVE-2024-21762; malware families: Cobalt Strike; threat actors: Volt Typhoon; vectors: exploit, vpn-edge; products: Fortinet FortiOS.

objectives.title: Anomalous remote logons (Type 3 / Type 10)
objectives.falsification_criterion: If 4624 logon-type 3/10 events show no bursts from a single source to many destinations, lateral movement via RDP/SMB is unsupported.
objectives.suggested_query: security | where event_id in (4624) and logon_type in (3,10) | summarize dests = dcount(dst_host) by src_user, src_host | where dests > 10

objectives.title: Admin-tool usage outside baseline
objectives.falsification_criterion: If PsExec / WMIC / PowerShell remoting / Impacket-style usage is absent outside known admin jump-hosts, the lateral-tool hypothesis is disproven.
objectives.suggested_query: process | where name in ('psexec.exe','psexesvc.exe','wmic.exe','wsmprovhost.exe') and host !in (admin_jumphosts)

objectives.title: Kerberos abuse telemetry
objectives.falsification_criterion: If 4769 ticket requests show no anomalous RC4 / odd-SPN patterns and no AS-REP roasting indicators, credential-based lateral movement is unsupported.
objectives.suggested_query: security | where event_id == 4769 and ticket_encryption == 'RC4-HMAC' | summarize by target_spn, account_name

objectives.title: Lateral file-copy staging
objectives.falsification_criterion: If SMB writes of archives / executables across multiple hosts from one user/host are absent, lateral staging is unsupported.
objectives.suggested_query: file | where action == 'write' and ext in ('.7z','.rar','.zip','.exe') and dest matches /\\\\.*\\(C\$|admin\$)/

article.title: Cl0p ransomware abuses CVE-2025-3104 in MOVEit Transfer for mass data theft
article.summary: The Cl0p ransomware crew is again exploiting a zero-day in MOVEit Transfer, this time CVE-2025-3104, to drop a webshell and exfiltrate data from managed file transfer instances at finance and healthcare organisations. Talos reports the use of a custom .NET webshell, archive staging with 7z, and exfiltration to transfer.sh and anonfiles.com. Observed IP: 91.219.236.50.

article.title: Akira ransomware operators exploit exposed Cisco ASA VPNs without MFA
article.summary: CISA and partners warn that Akira ransomware affiliates continue to gain initial access via Cisco ASA SSL VPN portals where MFA is not enforced, often using credentials obtained from RedLine and Lumma Stealer logs. Lateral movement is conducted with RDP and PsExec, followed by data exfiltration via Rclone to mega.nz and encryption of ESXi datastores. Manufacturing and healthcare sectors are heavily targeted. IOC IPs include 45.61.136.215 and 193.143.1.205.

objectives.title: Kerberos abuse telemetry

article.title: Scattered Spider runs MFA-fatigue and help-desk social engineering against US insurance firms
article.summary: Scattered Spider (aka Octo Tempest, Muddled Libra) is targeting US insurance firms with vishing calls to help desks, MFA push-bombing, and OAuth illicit-consent grants in Entra ID. After initial access the group deploys ScreenConnect and AnyDesk for persistence and exfiltrates data via mega.nz before deploying ransomware. The financial and insurance sector should consider this an active campaign.

article.title: BumbleBee loader returns with SocGholish fake-update lures dropping IcedID and Cobalt Strike
article.summary: Proofpoint and Unit42 observed renewed BumbleBee activity delivered via SocGholish (FakeUpdates) JavaScript injects on compromised WordPress sites. Post-execution, operators dropped IcedID and Cobalt Strike beacons configured for HTTPS C2. Persistence was established via scheduled tasks and a Run key. SHA256: 9c2f1a0b6d4e5f9a8b7c6d5e4f3a2b1c0d9e8f7a6b5c4d3e2f1a0b9c8d7e6f5a.

article.title: APT29 (Midnight Blizzard) compromises Microsoft 365 tenants via OAuth abuse and password spraying
article.summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has attributed a new wave of Microsoft 365 tenant compromises to APT29 (Midnight Blizzard / Cozy Bear). The Russian SVR-linked group is performing password spraying against legacy authentication endpoints, then granting itself illicit OAuth consent to read mail and files in Entra ID. Government and education sectors are most affected.
